chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Main Types of Real Estate

lessons.title: Under-Construction vs Ready-to-Move: The Risk and Price Trade-Off

children.text: Aditi and her brother Kunal both want a 2BHK in Wakad, Pune. Aditi books an under-construction flat for ₹85 lakh, with possession promised in three years. Kunal buys a ready-to-move flat of the same size in a completed society next door for ₹1 crore. Aditi feels she saved ₹15 lakh. Did she? That depends on GST, rent, delays and whether the developer delivers at all. By the end of this lesson, you will be able to put a number on that ₹15 lakh "saving."

body.text: The discount on an under-construction flat is not free money. It is your payment for waiting, for paying rent and EMIs at the same time, and for trusting a developer with your money before anything exists.

children.text: The Documents That Separate the Two

markDefs.definition: A certificate from the local authority confirming a building was constructed as per the approved plan and meets safety norms, so it can legally be occupied.
A certificate from the local authority confirming construction of a project is complete as per approved plans.

children.text: Legally, a flat is ready-to-move only when the building has an
Occupancy Certificate (OC)
, usually issued along with or after a
Completion Certificate (CC)

. A building that looks finished but has no OC is still, for tax, utility connections and legal purposes, not ready. Some developers hand over keys before the OC arrives. That is a red flag, not a shortcut.

cells: Usually lower than comparable ready flats
Higher, since the risk is already gone
You earn none and may pay rent elsewhere until possession
Move in or rent it out immediately
A brochure, a sample flat and a promise
The actual flat, society and neighbours
Delays or a stalled project are possible
Limited to what is left or on resale

children.text: The GST Gap

markDefs.definition: For GST purposes, a flat with a carpet area of up to 60 sq m in metro cities or 90 sq m elsewhere, priced at up to ₹45 lakh.

children.text: Buyers of under-construction homes pay GST of 5% on the agreement value, without input tax credit. For homes that qualify as
affordable housing

, the rate is 1%. Ready-to-move flats with an OC, and resale flats, attract no GST. These rates were left unchanged by the GST rate overhaul that took effect on 22 September 2025. For Aditi's ₹85 lakh flat, GST adds ₹4.25 lakh, cutting her headline ₹15 lakh saving to ₹10.75 lakh before anything else.

body.title: GST on an affordable home
body.prompt: A first-time buyer in Nagpur books an under-construction 2BHK priced at ₹42 lakh with a carpet area of 58 sq m. It qualifies as affordable housing. How much GST will the buyer pay, in ₹?
body.explanation: The flat meets both affordable housing tests (price up to ₹45 lakh, carpet area within the limit), so GST is 1%. ₹42,00,000 × 1% = ₹42,000. At ₹46 lakh, the same flat would attract 5%, or ₹2,30,000.

children.text: The Real Cost of Waiting

Aditi currently rents a flat for ₹22,000 a month. Until possession, she keeps paying that rent. Kunal moves into his flat immediately. Here is how the "saving" looks once GST and rent are counted. To keep the comparison simple, it ignores home loan interest and any price change over the period.

body.caption: What is left of Aditi's ₹15 lakh discount?

cells: Rent paid while waiting at ₹22,000 a month

body.title: Total cost of getting a 2BHK in Wakad (₹ lakh, illustrative)

children.text: If the project is delivered on time, Aditi keeps a cushion of about ₹2.83 lakh, a thin reward for three years of risk and for paying most of the price before she can use the flat. A two-year delay wipes it out and leaves her ₹2.45 lakh worse off than Kunal. If the flat appreciates while under construction, Aditi gains; if the project stalls, she can lose far more than rent.

body.title: Calculate the cushion
body.prompt: An under-construction flat in Kolar Road, Bhopal costs ₹88 lakh, while a comparable ready flat costs ₹1 crore. GST is 5%. The buyer pays rent of ₹18,000 a month for 30 months until possession. Ignoring loan interest and price changes, how much of the discount is left, in ₹ lakh?
body.explanation: Discount: ₹1 crore minus ₹88 lakh = ₹12 lakh. GST: ₹88 lakh × 5% = ₹4.4 lakh. Rent: ₹18,000 × 30 = ₹5.4 lakh. Cushion: ₹12 lakh minus ₹4.4 lakh minus ₹5.4 lakh = ₹2.2 lakh. A six-month delay would cost another ₹1.08 lakh in rent, cutting it to ₹1.12 lakh.

children.text: Delivery Risk Is Not Theoretical

stats.label: Homes completely stalled
stats.context: Roughly 28% of the delayed stock, ANAROCK, 2021

markDefs.definition: An arrangement where the developer pays the buyer's pre-EMI interest to the bank until possession, while the bank releases large parts of the loan to the developer early.

children.text: The damage was worst for buyers who used
subvention schemes

, marketed as "20:80" or "no EMI till possession." Banks released most of the loan to developers upfront. When developers stopped paying the interest, banks demanded EMIs from buyers for flats that did not exist.

body.text: Subvention schemes are now under criminal investigation. In July 2025, the CBI registered 22 cases and searched 47 locations across Delhi-NCR in cases involving builders accused of defrauding homebuyers. In September 2025, a three-judge Supreme Court bench directed the CBI to register a case and investigate the alleged nexus between builders, banks and housing finance companies. If an offer says "you pay nothing until possession," read the tripartite agreement: you are almost always liable for the loan if the developer defaults.

children.text: How RERA Protects Under-Construction Buyers
Registration and a committed date.
Projects covered by RERA must register with the state authority and declare a completion date before selling.
Ring-fenced money.
70% of the money collected from buyers must go into a separate bank account and be used only for that project's land and construction costs.
Capped advance.
A developer cannot take more than 10% of the price as an advance before a written agreement for sale is registered.
Compensation for delay.
If possession is late, the buyer can withdraw and get a refund with interest, or stay in the project and receive interest for every month of delay.
Defect liability.
The developer must fix structural defects and poor workmanship reported within five years of possession, at no cost to the buyer.

body.label: RERA's most important safeguard
body.context: Before RERA took full effect in 2017, many developers used buyer advances from one project to buy land for the next. The separate account rule was designed to stop exactly that.

body.text: RERA gives you legal rights, but it cannot create money from a developer that has run out of it. If a developer goes bankrupt, homebuyers are treated as financial creditors under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, which gives them a vote in the resolution process. That is still a long, uncertain road, often measured in years. The best protection is choosing a developer that is unlikely to need it.

children.text: Payment Plans and What They Signal

body.caption: Common payment plans for under-construction homes

cells: Payments due as each construction stage is completed, such as each floor slab
Payments due on fixed dates, regardless of progress
Medium: you can pay ahead of construction
Pay most of the price upfront for an extra discount
High: most of your money is exposed if the project stalls
Pay a small amount; the bank funds the rest early and the developer covers interest until possession
Highest: you owe the bank even if the developer defaults

body.text: A developer offering a large extra discount for paying 90% upfront, or aggressively pushing subvention plans, may be short of cash. Strong developers with healthy sales rarely need to pull buyer money forward. Treat unusually generous payment terms as a question about the developer's finances.

children.text: Which One Suits You?

columns.label: Under-construction can work if
points: The developer has a long record of on-time delivery and OCs in past projects
You already live somewhere stable and can afford rent and EMIs together
The discount to comparable ready flats is large enough to cover GST, rent and some delay
You pay through a construction-linked plan and can wait an extra year or two

columns.label: Ready-to-move is better if
points: You need to move in or earn rent soon
You cannot absorb rent plus EMIs for several years
The developer is new, small or has delayed projects before
You want to see the actual flat, the society's upkeep and the neighbourhood first

body.title: Does GST apply?
body.question: Meera buys a flat in a Gurugram project where the Occupancy Certificate was issued two months before she signed the sale deed. What GST does she pay on the flat's price?
body.explanation: Once the Occupancy Certificate is issued before the sale, the flat is treated as ready-to-move, and no GST applies. She still pays stamp duty and registration charges.

body.title: The key certificate
body.textWithBlank: A flat is legally ready-to-move only after the local authority issues an ___ Certificate, confirming it can be lived in.
body.explanation: The Occupancy Certificate confirms the building meets approved plans and safety norms. Without it, the flat attracts GST as under-construction, and permanent utility connections can be a problem.

body.title: The "no EMI till possession" offer
body.scenario: Farhan and Zoya, both working in Noida, are offered a 3BHK in an under-construction project in Greater Noida West for ₹92 lakh. The developer's offer: pay just 20% now, the bank funds 80%, and the developer pays all interest until possession in 2029. The developer is mid-sized and one of its earlier projects was delivered about 18 months late. A comparable ready 3BHK nearby costs ₹1.05 crore.
body.prompt: Should they take the offer? What should they check or change?
body.modelAnswer:
1. The structure is a subvention plan: if the developer stops paying interest, the bank will demand EMIs from Farhan and Zoya, even with no flat. They must read the tripartite agreement closely.
2. Track record: an 18-month delay in an earlier project is a real warning sign. They should check that project's OC status and the RERA quarterly progress updates for this one.
3. The numbers: the discount is ₹13 lakh. GST at 5% on ₹92 lakh is ₹4.6 lakh. If they pay ₹20,000 a month in rent for three years, that is ₹7.2 lakh, leaving a cushion of only about ₹1.2 lakh. Just six months of delay (₹1.2 lakh more rent) wipes it out.
4. Who ultimately pays for the "free" interest: it is usually built into the price. They should ask for the price under a normal construction-linked plan instead.
5. Legal context: subvention schemes in Delhi-NCR are under CBI investigation after Supreme Court directions in 2025. That alone justifies extreme caution.
6. A reasonable conclusion: either decline, or negotiate a construction-linked plan with a larger discount, and compare seriously with the ₹1.05 crore ready flat, which carries no GST, no rent overlap and no delivery risk.

body.title: Before Booking an Under-Construction Flat
steps: Find the project on the state RERA website and read its quarterly progress updates
Check the developer's last three projects: were they delivered on time, and do they have OCs?
Compare the price with nearby ready flats, after adding GST and rent until possession
Add a buffer of at least 12 to 24 months of delay to your calculations
Insist on a construction-linked payment plan
Read the agreement for sale and any tripartite loan agreement before paying more than 10%
Confirm who the project's lender is and whether the land title is clear

body.label: Karnataka RERA: Project Search
body.description: Search registered projects, completion dates and progress disclosures. Every state has a similar RERA portal.

cards.definition: A local authority certificate confirming a building can legally be occupied.
A local authority certificate confirming construction is complete as per approved plans.
5% on under-construction flats, 1% on affordable housing, and none on ready flats with an OC or on resale.
A payment plan where instalments fall due only as construction stages are completed.
A 20:80 or no-EMI-till-possession plan where the bank funds the developer early and the developer pays interest; the buyer remains liable if the developer defaults.
The rule that 70% of buyer money must be kept in a dedicated account for that project's land and construction costs.

points: An under-construction discount pays you for waiting, for delivery risk and for paying before you can use the flat.
GST of 5% (1% for affordable homes) applies to under-construction flats; ready flats with an OC attract none.
In our Wakad example, GST and three years of rent shrank a ₹15 lakh discount to ₹2.83 lakh, and a two-year delay turned it negative.
Stalled and delayed projects are a real risk: ANAROCK counted 6.29 lakh such homes in the top seven cities in 2021.
RERA ring-fences 70% of buyer money, caps advances at 10% and pays interest for delays, but cannot rescue a developer that has run out of money.
Prefer construction-linked plans and developers with proven delivery, and treat subvention and heavy upfront payment offers with great caution.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment, legal or tax advice. GST, RERA rules and payment practices can change and may vary by state and project. Examples use illustrative prices and rents. Consult a qualified property lawyer, a tax professional and a SEBI-registered investment adviser before making investment decisions.
